predictions.title: Durable agent-execution substrate hardens into a standard primitive by H1 2027
predictions.body: Two June launches landed within a day of each other and split the autonomous-coding-agent field along a single axis - not model quality, but where the long-running agent physically executes. On June 11 OpenAI acquired Ona, the rebranded Gitpod, and folded it into the Codex group precisely to run agents inside persistent cloud sandboxes that keep multi-day coding tasks alive after the developer's workstation powers off, with European trade coverage framing the durable, restart-surviving execution layer as the workflow Anthropic already dominates in the enterprise and the thing OpenAI is buying infrastructure and talent to contest. On June 12 Moonshot shipped Kimi Work, a downloadable desktop agent that takes the opposite bet: an always-on local Agent Swarm of roughly 300 sub-agents on the open-weight Kimi K2.6, driving the user's logged-in browser through a WebBridge extension and firing overnight jobs through a built-in cron engine with a keep-awake toggle - and the same K2.6 weights are already runnable on-device through Unsloth's 2-bit dynamic quant, so the local-execution story is not aspirational. The shared move is that long-horizon autonomy is being re-architected around a durable execution substrate that survives the session, and the contest is consolidating around who owns that substrate rather than who has the better model. The forward thesis is that this durable agent-execution layer stops being two vendors' bespoke plumbing and hardens into a named, expected primitive that a buyer assumes any serious coding-agent product ships. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by H1 2027 at least one additional major lab or coding-agent harness (the strongest candidates being Anthropic, Google, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Cognition/Devin, or a frontier Chinese lab such as Alibaba/Qwen, DeepSeek, or Zhipu) ships - as a documented, generally available product feature, not a preview teaser or blog mention - EITHER a durable cloud-sandbox execution mode where an agent task continues running and is resumable after the user's client disconnects or the local machine is shut down, OR a packaged local persistent-agent runtime that runs a multi-agent swarm on the user's own machine with scheduled/overnight execution and resumable long-horizon runs. A pure model-capability release with no durable-execution surface, a chat product that merely lengthens a single in-session run without disconnect survival or resumability, or a closed private beta with no GA path does not count; the marker is a third independent shipped durable-execution substrate (cloud-sandbox or local-swarm) beyond OpenAI/Ona and Moonshot/Kimi Work. If by June 30, 2027 no additional major lab or harness has shipped such a generally available durable-execution mode and the pattern remains confined to these two vendors, the prediction fails.

reasoning.because: OpenAI bought Ona for persistent cloud sandboxes; Moonshot shipped local-swarm Kimi Work (Jun 11-12)
reasoning.given: the agent contest is shifting from model quality to who owns the restart-surviving execution layer
reasoning.so_that: a third major lab or harness ships a generally available durable-execution substrate - cloud-sandbox or local-swarm
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027: a 3rd lab/harness ships cloud-sandbox or local-swarm durable agents
reasoning.plain_language: Two AI makers just shipped robots that keep working after you close your laptop; soon a third copies the idea as a normal feature.

predictions.summary: OpenAI's June 11 Ona buy (persistent cloud sandboxes) and Moonshot's June 12 Kimi Work (a 300-agent local swarm) split coding agents on where they run, moving the contest to who owns the restart-surviving execution layer. Expect a third major lab or harness to ship that durable substrate by H1 2027.

predictions.title: SSM-hybrid open-weight VLMs harden into an established edge category by Q2 2027
predictions.body: Zyphra's June 12 release of Zamba2-VL under Apache 2.0 is the moment the state-space-hybrid backbone crossed from text into open-weight multimodal at sizes that actually fit local hardware. The family ships at 1.2B, 2.7B, and 7B with checkpoints on Hugging Face: the language backbone interleaves Mamba2 state-space layers with a small number of shared transformer blocks, and the vision side reuses the Vision Transformer from Qwen2.5-VL through a two-layer MLP adapter. The payoff is latency - on a 32K-token prefill Zyphra measures roughly an order-of-magnitude lower time-to-first-token than comparable transformer VLMs, the regime that decides whether on-device document and screen understanding feels instant - and the small models are not merely competitive but strong on perception, with the 1.2B variant reaching PixMoCount 62.5, nearly double the transformer-based InternVL3.5-1B at 32.8, and the 2.7B/7B variants posting CountBenchQA 87.5 and 90.6. Two things make this a seed rather than a one-off. First, the value proposition is structural, not incidental: linear-time state-space attention is exactly what removes the quadratic prefill cost that makes long-context, image-heavy VLMs slow on edge silicon, so the architecture's advantage compounds precisely where local multimodal inference is headed. Second, the field has exactly one open-weight SSM-hybrid VLM family today, and the on-device runtime stack that actually deploys 1-7B weights locally - llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio - has no first-class path for the Mamba2-hybrid VLM graph, so the format ships against an ecosystem not yet built to run it. The forward thesis is that the SSM-hybrid multimodal backbone hardens into an established open-weight edge category rather than remaining a single Zyphra checkpoint. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by Q2 2027 EITHER a second independent open-weight SSM-hybrid (Mamba/state-space) vision-language model family ships with its own model card and downloadable weights under a permissive or open license from a non-Zyphra publisher (the strongest candidates being Alibaba/Qwen, Mistral, NVIDIA, AI21, or a Mamba-lineage group), OR a mainstream on-device/edge inference runtime that did not support it at Zamba2-VL's launch - llama.cpp foremost, or Ollama, LM Studio, or MLX as a packaged GGUF/edge path - ships first-class support for the Mamba2-hybrid VLM path so the model runs natively on the consumer/edge stack. A pure-text SSM model with no vision tower, a research-only paper with no released weights, a further Zyphra follow-up checkpoint, or a runtime that merely wraps the existing custom transformers fork without native Mamba2-hybrid VLM support does not count; the marker is a second independent open-weight SSM-hybrid VLM family or genuine edge-runtime support for the hybrid multimodal graph. If by June 30, 2027 Zamba2-VL is still the only open-weight SSM-hybrid VLM family and no mainstream on-device runtime has shipped first-class support for the Mamba2-hybrid VLM path, the prediction fails.

reasoning.because: Zyphra shipped Zamba2-VL June 12, the first open-weight Mamba2-hybrid VLM family at 1-7B edge sizes
reasoning.given: state-space attention kills quadratic prefill cost, but no edge runtime runs the hybrid VLM graph
reasoning.so_that: a second open-weight SSM-hybrid VLM family ships, or a mainstream edge runtime adds Mamba2-hybrid VLM support
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027: a second SSM-hybrid VLM family, or on-device runtime support for it
reasoning.plain_language: Zyphra made the first open vision AI on a fast new design that fits small devices; soon a rival copies it or apps run it.

predictions.summary: Zyphra's June 12 Zamba2-VL is the first open-weight Mamba2-hybrid VLM family, cutting time-to-first-token by about an order of magnitude at 1-7B edge sizes while beating transformer baselines on counting. Expect the SSM-hybrid backbone to become an established open-weight edge category by Q2 2027.

predictions.title: A frontier AI lab files a public S-1 and prices its IPO by Q2 2027
predictions.body: The frontier-lab path to public markets turned concrete this week. Anthropic confidentially filed a draft Form S-1 with the SEC on June 1 - on the back of a $65B round at a $965B post-money valuation and an annualized revenue run-rate that crossed $47B (more than tripled since February) - explicitly setting up an IPO that pits it against OpenAI, which is targeting a raise of at least $60B at a valuation of up to $1 trillion and is expected to list by year's end. The ceiling for how much public-market capital a single high-multiple technology name can absorb just reset: on June 11 SpaceX priced 555.6 million shares at $135 apiece to raise about $75B, the largest IPO in history, demonstrating live appetite for an outsized private-tech debut. The forward thesis is that this confidential, paper-stage maneuvering converts into an actual public offering. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by Q2 2027 at least one of the two largest labs - Anthropic or OpenAI - publicly files a non-confidential Form S-1 (or its F-1 / 424B equivalent), sets a price range or final per-share terms, and prices the offering ahead of a first trade on a US exchange (NYSE or Nasdaq), confirmed via the SEC EDGAR public filing plus an on-record pricing press release or exchange listing notice. The doesn't-count set is explicit: a confidential or draft S-1 alone (the June 1 status) does not count; neither does a further private round, a directing-bank mandate, an analyst report, an exchange reservation of a ticker, or an indicative range that is withdrawn before pricing. What counts is a public registration that proceeds to set terms and price - the moment the lab commits to selling shares to public investors at a stated price. The counter-risk is that a private-market round at SpaceX-scale valuations, or a regulatory or market-window stall, lets both labs stay private through mid-2027, leaving the confidential filing as the furthest either gets.

reasoning.because: June 1: Anthropic confidentially filed a draft S-1 ($965B post-money); OpenAI prepping its listing
reasoning.given: SpaceX's June 11 $75B pricing at $135/share reset the ceiling for public capital in one tech name
reasoning.so_that: Anthropic or OpenAI converts a draft filing into a public, non-confidential S-1 that sets terms and prices an IPO
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; Anthropic or OpenAI public S-1 + priced offering on NYSE/Nasdaq
reasoning.plain_language: Anthropic secretly filed to go public and OpenAI is getting ready too; soon one of them will openly sell shares at a set price.

predictions.summary: Anthropic confidentially filed a draft S-1 on June 1 ($965B post-money), OpenAI is preparing its own listing, and SpaceX's $75B June 11 pricing proved public-market appetite. Expect Anthropic or OpenAI to file a non-confidential S-1 and price an IPO by Q2 2027; a confidential draft does not count.
